summary: Quarterly renewal check-in focused on capacity uplift and multi-region activation. Customer wants to add EU private pilot and APAC burst capacity while negotiating a 12-month renewal. Discussed latency goals, data residency, KMS/HSM integration, and options for Dedicated reserved pools vs hosted tier burst. Agreed on benchmarks, updated pricing, and next steps for pilot kickoff.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-26
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Lucas Ortega (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (VantageRx Head of MLOps), Sofia Martinez (VantageRx CTO), Naomi Ito (VantageRx Cloud Eng)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Raj Patel: Raj here.
[00:09] Sofia Martinez: Sofia on my side.
[00:11] Naomi Ito: Naomi, hi.
[00:13] Lucas Ortega: Lucas from Redwood.
[00:15] Maya Chen: Great. So agenda — renewal check-in, capacity uplift, EU private pilot ask, a bit on APAC burst. We'll keep it informal, we'll take notes, and I'll follow up with pricing and links.

[00:28] Raj Patel: Sounds good. Quick context — we're up for re-up in June, roughly 12 months. Usage in prod has been steady, peak days spiky. We're seeing more EU traffic after the new partner launch and need to explore residency. Also APAC has seasonal bursts.

[00:42] Maya Chen: Understood. On the renewal front are you looking to change commitment levels or just add regions?
[00:46] Raj Patel: Both. We want a modest commitment bump — maybe 20–30% baseline — and a reserve for burst in APAC, plus an EU private pilot to keep PII in-region.

[00:55] Lucas Ortega: Quick technical flag — EU private pilot can be VPC-hosted private plane or onprem. There are different timelines. Onprem lead time tends to be 6–8 weeks for full provisioning and testing, VPC private is faster.

[01:14] Sofia Martinez: For us, timeline matters — legal wants EU residency before end of Q3. Onprem is preferred but we can do VPC if the audit trail and KMS meet our requirements. Does Redwood support customer-managed KMS/HSM for private deployments?

[01:28] Lucas Ortega: Yes, we have KMS integrations for private deployments and HSM options in the onprem package. Though the HSM path requires an ops checklist and a short security review. We can share the SOC2 + ISO docs; I will note that there's sometimes minor differences in the audit evidence for hosted vs private.

[01:45] Naomi Ito: Also need clarity on network egress — if we go VPC-private is egress billed differently? And what's the monitoring surface for tokens and cost breakdown?

[01:55] Maya Chen: Good Q. For VPC-private, egress depends on the cloud provider and will show in separate line items. In the Console you'll get token-level breakdowns and per-route latency and cost — Lucas can show an example.

[02:10] Lucas Ortega: I'll grab a screenshot after. For cost engineering, we recommend configuring prefix caching and KV cache for the top 5 prompt families — that usually cuts 20–40% token usage on chat flows.

[02:22] Raj Patel: Hmm okay. We have a lot of repeated system prompts and patient histories in the prompts. Caching might help. But we need to validate quality — can't have hallucinations due to aggressive quant.

[02:33] Lucas Ortega: Totally — caching is orthogonal to quantization. For quant we recommend per-model quant profiles; Redwood Optimize can suggest profiles based on your evals. We'll avoid any aggressive 4-bit profiles on mission-critical prompts without an eval pass.

[02:48] Sofia Martinez: Can you spell that out — what does the Dedicated reserved pool give us vs hosted burst? We're worried about latency during peak.

[02:56] Maya Chen: Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolated capacity. Latency SLOs are stricter — we can configure pinned model variants and autoscale policies. Hosted is flexible and cheaper for baseline but may fall back to lower-tier variants under extreme load unless you lock in reserved capacity.

[03:12] Raj Patel: Our latency SLO is 300ms p95 for short chat completions (<128 tokens). Can Redwood meet that from EU and APAC?

[03:20] Lucas Ortega: From EU, yes with dedicated capacity in an EU geocluster and optimized kernels; APAC is possible with an APAC edge or burst nodes. But we need to run a representative benchmark with your actual payloads because sequence lengths and cache hit rates change the numbers.

[03:35] Naomi Ito: We'll share payloads — but what's a realistic test window and what metrics will you deliver?

[03:40] Lucas Ortega: We'll do a 1-hour sustained load and a 30-minute spike. Deliverables: p50/p90/p95 latencies, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and a recommended batch size + kernel config. I can run that against both hosted and a narrow dedicated config if you give us the payloads.

[03:58] Maya Chen: Great — that's one of the action items.

[04:02] Sofia Martinez: Security — besides SOC2, we need audit logs for every inference call and RBAC integration with our SSO. Are those available in private?

[04:11] Lucas Ortega: Yes — private control plane surfaces audit logs with request-level metadata. RBAC and SAML/Sso integrations are supported for the console and keys. There might be additional config steps for onprem to point to your IDP.

[04:24] Raj Patel: Pricing — what's the friction going from hosted to dedicated? Is there a conversion/migration cost?

[04:30] Maya Chen: There's an onboarding fee for Dedicated provisioning and SLA enablement. We'll include it in the quote. Also term commitments reduce the unit token cost. We can model a 12-month vs 24-month all-in TCO.

[04:40] Raj Patel: We may also evaluate a hybrid: baseline on hosted + reserved Dedicated pool during business hours in EU, burst to hosted in APAC nights. Is that supported?

[04:49] Lucas Ortega: Absolutely, smart routing supports policy-based routing by region/time/cost. You can set primary route to Dedicated EU and fallback to hosted variants. We also have automatic model fallback to lighter quantized variants if capacity constrained.

[05:05] Naomi Ito: Any caveats with model state / KV cache when routing across variants?

[05:09] Lucas Ortega: Cross-variant routing may invalidate some KV caches; we recommend sticky routing per session for chat that uses long-term KV. There are prefix caching strategies to mitigate warm-up.

[05:21] Maya Chen: Ok quick commercial check — you said 20–30% uplift. Do you have an initial number for tokens/day?

[05:27] Raj Patel: Our average is about 150M tokens/day currently, peak 220M on partner days. Forecast for Q4 if we launch EU pilot is +40% peak.

[05:38] Maya Chen: Thanks — that helps. We'll model 200M baseline with a 300M peak bucket for APAC bursts.

[05:45] Sofia Martinez: Can you also outline the rollback/fallback plan if the EU pilot has issues? We need a fail-safe to keep production sane.

[05:53] Lucas Ortega: Yes — can do canary routes and automatic rollback. We have A/B rollouts and immediate fallback to hosted gov variants. We'll document the steps and a runbook.

[06:05] Raj Patel: On the legal side, our counsel asked about data retention for debug logs — can we have short retention for PII logs and longer for non-PII?

[06:13] Maya Chen: In private deployments you can configure retention windows and redaction. For hosted we offer retention tiers but there's a standard default; we'd have to document redaction guarantees. I'll pull the security doc with that callout.

[06:26] Sofia Martinez: One competitor brought up lower unit costs but limited observability. For us visibility is huge. What additional monitoring level can we get?

[06:34] Lucas Ortega: We can expose token-level traces, per-prompt SLO dashboards, and custom traces to your APM via tracing hooks. There's also drift/quality alerts tied to eval sets.

[06:47] Raj Patel: Ok that's good. I want to make sure quantization won't be autopiloted — any changes to model variants are via staged rollouts and require our sign-off?

[06:56] Maya Chen: Yes, rollout can be manual or Canary. Redwood Optimize recommendations are just that — suggestions. You control the rollout and we can lock changes behind approval gates.

[07:07] Naomi Ito: For the EU onprem pilot — what's a realistic timeline if we start provisioning in mid-April?

[07:12] Lucas Ortega: If provisioning begins mid-April, we'd aim for staging by late May and a short acceptance window in early June — assuming quick legal and infra access. Onprem tends to take a bit longer for certs and HSM work.

[07:25] Raj Patel: That meets our Q3 residency ask if acceptance in June.

[07:30] Maya Chen: Next up — benchmarks. Action item for Lucas to run the bench after Naomi shares payloads. We'll also send an updated pricing worksheet modeling baseline + burst and Dedicated onboarding fee.

[07:42] Sofia Martinez: Please include a per-token and per-hour breakdown and a scenario showing 12-month and 24-month committed terms.

[07:49] Maya Chen: Will do. We'll also add an option for a short pilot discount for the first 2 months of EU onprem.

[07:58] Raj Patel: That helps. Any gotchas we should watch for when migrating session state?

[08:03] Lucas Ortega: Watch for session affinity and prefix cache warmup. Also if you use fine-grained KV per tenant, ensure the storage backend is sized appropriately. We'll include sizing recommendations.

[08:15] Maya Chen: Alright, to recap quickly before we end —
[08:18] Maya Chen: 1) Redwood to send capacity/price spreadsheet and Dedicated onboarding fees by 2026-04-02.
[08:24] Maya Chen: 2) Naomi to share token histograms, top prompt families by 2026-04-05.
[08:29] Maya Chen: 3) Lucas to run latency/throughput benchmark using customer payloads and share results by 2026-04-07.
[08:36] Maya Chen: 4) Schedule EU onprem pilot kickoff targeted week of 2026-04-12 (depends on legal/ops).

[08:42] Raj Patel: Good. Also please include a short runbook for rollback and an example canary policy.

[08:47] Maya Chen: Noted — will include.

[08:50] Sofia Martinez: One last thing — can you attach the security pack and the recent benchmark we ran with another customer? We want to compare.

[08:56] Lucas Ortega: I'll attach SOC2, ISO, and a sanitized benchmark PDF plus a short spreadsheet with kernel configs.

[09:04] Maya Chen: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the doc pack and the spreadsheet. If anything pops up, reach out on the thread.

[09:10] Raj Patel: Thanks everyone.
[09:12] Meeting ended.

Notes on transcription quality: names occasionally merged (e.g., VantageRx sometimes heard as Vantage-R X), some technical terms transcribed roughly (HSM -> H-S-M, geocluster -> geo-cluckster), punctuation and sentence boundaries are approximate.
